blind_spots.blind_spot: Data pipeline depends on consumer cloud sync
blind_spots.operator_reality: A casualty-collection point or far-forward aid station has no commercial internet; a device that can't log locally-first and only syncs later becomes a black box exactly when the medic needs the data most.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Built for a research/clinical-trial workflow (UAB Hospital, MATLAB/Python analysis) before it was hardened for the DDIL environment the SBIR abstract itself describes.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Log files are synchronized to your iCloud

blind_spots.blind_spot: Command app is tied to a commercial iOS ecosystem, not the TAK stack
blind_spots.operator_reality: Operators already run ATAK/TAK for situational awareness; a separate Apple-only companion app means a second device, second battery, and a workflow break at exactly the moment BATDOK is trying to unify casualty data into one picture.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team is materials-science/mechanical-engineering-led (Soft Machines Lab, CMU) — strong on the wearable sensor, but the site never mentions ATAK/TAK despite integrating with a situational-awareness-adjacent tool (BATDOK).
blind_spots.evidence_quote: ProPatch™ Connect Available on the Apple App Store

blind_spots.blind_spot: No visible ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR posture despite handling casualty PHI on a DoD network-integrated device
blind_spots.operator_reality: BATDOK integration means ProPatch data eventually touches a government network; without an ATO package or a named compliance owner, the device can demo at AFRL all day and still get stopped cold at the accreditation gate before fielding.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company is 4 PhD/academic cofounders plus a Government Sales Manager hire — no compliance/ISSO role visible, and site language never uses ATO/RMF/CMMC/STIG anywhere across 1258 words.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Central Monitoring Made Easy Apply ProPatch to each patient, and monitor from one place

opener_hook: Your ProPatch-BATDOK integration is already running with AFRL's 711th Human Performance Wing — but the log files syncing to iCloud assume connectivity a far-forward casualty collection point won't have.
what_they_do: A wireless chest-worn patient monitor (ProPatch) for combat medics, integrated with the Air Force's BATDOK triage app, using ML to classify casualty health state at point of injury.
